newsitem.title: USA: Western Digital up after higher earnings.
newsitem.headline: Western Digital up after higher earnings.

text.p: Western Digital Corp shares rose to a new high Thursday, one day after the computer disk drive maker reported much better-than-expected first-quarter earnings.
Shares of Western Digital, based in Irvine, Calif., were up 3-3/8 to 45-1/2 in New York Stock Exchange trading. Earlier, the shares traded as high as 50, topping the previous 52-week high of 46-3/4.
The shares of other disk drive manufacturers and components makers -- including Seagate Technology Inc and Read-Rite Corp -- also rose.
Analysts said Western Digital likely will continue to report sharply higher earnings in the next few quarters amid strong sales of disk drives to personal computer makers.

"They are in great shape," said David Kerdell, an analyst at Oppenheimer in New York. "Western Digital has been taking market share from its competitors. Their unit shipments were up 75 percent in the quarter from a year ago."

Western Digital makes disk drives, the devices in personal computers that store information permanently. In recent quarters, the company has been able to introduce high-capacity drives at competitive prices.
Strong sales of disk drives for personal computers accounted for the company's sharply higher first-quarter earnings, Kerdell said.

After the market closed yesterday, Western Digital, based in Irvine, Calif., said earnings for the quarter ended Sept. 28 almost quadrupled to $32.9 million, or $0.70 a diluted share, from $8.33 million shares, or $0.16. First-quarter revenue rose 58 percent to $883.1 million from $558.1 million.
According to First Call, the company was expected to report a profit of $0.49 a share in the first quarter.
